title: SSR, SSG, ISR and dynamic rendering
description: Compare static, incremental, and server-rendered strategies so you can choose the right one for each page.

data.text: Not every page needs the same freshness. A marketing page may change once a month. A dashboard must show the latest data. Next.js gives you four rendering strategies: **Static Site Generation (SSG)**, **Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)**, **Server-Side Rendering (SSR)**, and **Dynamic Rendering**.

In the App Router, these strategies are mostly automatic. The framework looks at your data-fetching code, caching headers, and cookies to decide whether a page can be cached or must render fresh. You do not usually set a global mode. Instead, you opt into dynamic behavior where needed.

rows: Build time, then on-demand or time-based
Per request, often with uncached data

data.title: How Next.js decides
data.text: If a page uses `fetch` with `next: { revalidate }`, Next.js may cache it. If it reads cookies, headers, or uses `searchParams`, it is usually treated as dynamic. If it calls a database without caching, it renders on every request.

data.content: Regenerate the page in the background every hour.

data.title: Dynamic page with searchParams
Key takeaway
points: SSG is fastest but only works for content that does not change per request.
ISR gives you fresh data without sacrificing full static speed.
SSR and Dynamic Rendering are for personalized or unpredictable data.
data.takeaway: Prefer cached rendering unless the page genuinely needs per-request freshness.
